findings.reason: the node would either be dispatched with one goal and reject the station work it is also graded on, or be re-opened by a station publication bug it never claimed to fix.
findings.text: §73's Done when carries a second, independent deliverable: "restarts the station partway through a tick and reads the queued count its first published tick reports equal to the count of queued requests in the store", where the store is the admission service's and the publishing process is the station; the Deliverable's own sentence bounds the count a reader sees after the service restarts, so a station publication defect can fail the node whose goal is that a kill loses no request, and neither clause can be closed on one verdict

findings.reason: the station clause has no evidence it can be red, so a node closing on it proves nothing about the publication behaviour it was added for.
findings.text: §73's negative control reads "at the base revision at least one stage leaves a request absent, stranded or launched twice", which the four SIGKILL stages satisfy on their own, so the station-restart test is never made to fail at base and the plan records no reason to believe it can fail at head; if the base station already publishes the store's count the clause passes on unfixed code and measures nothing

findings.reason: an idle hour closes the clause, so the section can be declared done without the fleet-level behaviour it was written for ever being observed.
findings.text: §74's third measure, "a census on the fleet node one hour after landing finds no worker process whose run reads terminal for more than one minute", is a snapshot with no population floor and no base arm: an hour in which no worker reaches a terminal phase satisfies it, and the clause cannot be run at base at all, so the only two measures that can be shown red are the tests; the deliverable's actual quantity — that every terminal run's tree is gone within a minute — is never counted over a population

findings.reason: the 3.5 GB item into the plan already undertakes to remove, and the test as written would not detect it, so the fixture needs imas-codex named to make the clause measurable.
findings.text: §71's Deliverable extends the exclusion to "any other server the user's or project's harness configuration names, such as imas-codex serve, which reckon-af's census ... found under 12 workers at 3.5 GB", but its Done when seeds a user configuration naming only reckon, imas-dd and lucy2 and asserts a project-side declaration only implicitly, while the landed fence already disables every undeclared project server (`tests/test_worker_mcp_servers.py:168`), so the one server the Why prices has no case — a launch that still carries imas-codex from the user configuration passes the stated assertion

findings.reason: without a named record the census is unreadable after the fact and the section's second quantity cannot be re-checked by anyone, which is the state a durable-evidence requirement exists to prevent.
findings.text: §74 makes a fleet census one hour after landing a done-when quantity but names a log only for its failing test run (`docs/evidence/fragments/work-flows-to-the-lane/s74.html`); the census's own output has no declared durable path, so a later reader cannot open the record the node closed on
